en.title: Legal guarantee
en.alt: Legal guarantee: EU harmonised notice on the legal guarantee of conformity
text: LEGAL GUARANTEE
Minimum two-year legal guarantee protection for goods sold in the European Union.
Consumers can claim their rights under the legal guarantee of conformity, for example if goods:
do not match the description;
do not function as intended.

Sellers are liable for any lack of conformity which existed when the goods were delivered, and which becomes apparent within the legal guarantee period. Sellers in such a situation are required to offer:
free repair or free replacement;
in some cases, a price reduction or full reimbursement.
Some countries have a longer legal guarantee period. For second-hand goods, a shorter period may apply, but not less than one year.
For more information on your rights in a specific country, scan the QR code below or ask the seller.
europa.eu/youreurope/guarantees
What to do if you receive non-conforming goods:
1. Contact the seller as soon as possible to report the issue;
2. Provide proof of purchase, such as a receipt, invoice, or bank statement.

Sellers and producers may also offer commercial guarantees, which apply independently from the legal guarantee. For example, you may see this GARAN label representing a commercial guarantee of durability offered by the producer at no additional cost and covering the entire good.

de.title: Gesetzliche Gewährleistung
de.alt: Gesetzliche Gewährleistung: harmonisierter EU-Hinweis zur gesetzlichen Gewährleistung
text: GESETZLICHE GEWÄHRLEISTUNG
Mindestens zwei Jahre gesetzliche Gewährleistung der Vertragsmäßigkeit für Waren, die in der Europäischen Union verkauft werden.
Verbraucherinnen und Verbraucher können ihre Rechte im Rahmen des gesetzlichen Gewährleistungsrechts geltend machen, z. B. wenn die Waren
nicht der Beschreibung entsprechen,
nicht bestimmungsgemäß funktionieren.

Verkäufer haften für jede Vertragswidrigkeit, die zum Zeitpunkt der Lieferung der Waren bestand und innerhalb des Zeitraums der gesetzlichen Gewährleistung erkennbar wird. Verkäufer müssen in solchen Fällen Folgendes anbieten:
kostenlose Nachbesserung oder kostenlose Ersatzlieferung,
in bestimmten Fällen eine Preisminderung oder eine vollständige Erstattung des Kaufpreises.
In einigen Ländern gilt ein längerer Zeitraum für die gesetzliche Gewährleistung. Für gebrauchte Waren kann ein kürzerer Zeitraum gelten, jedoch nicht weniger als ein Jahr.
Für weitere Informationen zu Ihren Rechten in einem bestimmten Land scannen Sie den nachstehenden QR-Code oder fragen Sie den Verkäufer.
europa.eu/youreurope/garantien
Was ist zu tun, wenn Sie vertragswidrige Waren erhalten?
1. Melden Sie dem Verkäufer das Problem so bald wie möglich.
2. Legen Sie einen Kaufnachweis vor, z. B. die Quittung, Rechnung oder einen Kontoauszug.

Verkäufer und Hersteller können auch gewerbliche Garantien gewähren, die unabhängig von der gesetzlichen Gewährleistung gelten. Diese GARAN-Kennzeichnung zeigt beispielsweise, dass der Hersteller eine gewerbliche Haltbarkeitsgarantie ohne zusätzliche Kosten gewährt, die die gesamte Ware abdeckt.

fr.title: Garantie légale
fr.alt: Garantie légale : avis harmonisé de l’UE sur la garantie légale de conformité
text: GARANTIE LÉGALE
Protection offerte par la garantie légale minimale de deux ans sur des biens vendus dans l’Union européenne.
Les consommateurs peuvent faire valoir leurs droits au titre de la garantie légale de conformité, par exemple si les biens:
ne correspondent pas à la description;
ne fonctionnent pas comme prévu.

Les vendeurs sont responsables de tout défaut de conformité qui existait au moment de la livraison des biens et qui apparaît pendant la période de garantie légale. Les vendeurs se trouvant dans une telle situation sont tenus de proposer:
une réparation gratuite ou un remplacement gratuit;
dans certains cas, une réduction de prix ou un remboursement intégral.
Dans certains pays, la période de garantie légale est plus longue. Pour les biens d’occasion, une période plus courte peut s’appliquer, mais elle ne peut être inférieure à un an.
Pour en savoir plus sur vos droits dans un pays donné, scannez le code QR ci-dessous ou consultez le vendeur.
europa.eu/youreurope/garanties
Que faire si vous recevez des biens non conformes:
1. contactez le vendeur dès que possible pour signaler le problème;
2. fournissez une preuve d’achat, telle qu’un reçu, une facture ou un relevé bancaire.

Les vendeurs et les producteurs peuvent également offrir des garanties commerciales, qui s’appliquent indépendamment de la garantie légale. Par exemple, il se peut que votre bien affiche ce label GARAN, représentant une garantie commerciale de durabilité offerte par le producteur sans frais supplémentaires et s’appliquant à l’ensemble du bien.

it.title: Garanzia legale
it.alt: Garanzia legale: avviso armonizzato UE sulla garanzia legale di conformità
text: GARANZIA LEGALE
Garanzia legale minima di due anni per i beni venduti nell’Unione europea.
I consumatori possono far valere i loro diritti nell’ambito della garanzia legale di conformità, ad esempio se i beni:
non corrispondono alla descrizione;
non funzionano come previsto.

I venditori sono responsabili di qualsiasi difetto di conformità esistente al momento della consegna dei beni e che si manifesta entro il periodo della garanzia legale. In tal caso i venditori sono tenuti a offrire:
la riparazione o sostituzione gratuita;
in alcuni casi, una riduzione del prezzo o il rimborso integrale.
Alcuni paesi prevedono un periodo di garanzia legale più lungo. Per i beni di seconda mano può valere un periodo più breve, ma non inferiore a un anno.
Per saperne di più sui propri diritti in un determinato paese, scansionare il codice QR qui sotto o chiedere informazioni al venditore.
europa.eu/youreurope/garanzie
Cosa fare se si ricevono beni non conformi:
1. contattare quanto prima il venditore per segnalare il problema;
2. fornire la prova dell’acquisto, ad esempio una ricevuta, una fattura o un estratto conto bancario.

I venditori e i produttori possono anche offrire garanzie commerciali, che si applicano indipendentemente dalla garanzia legale. Ad esempio, questa etichetta GARAN rappresenta una garanzia commerciale di durabilità offerta dal produttore senza costi aggiuntivi, che copre il bene nel suo complesso.

nl.title: Wettelijke garantie
nl.alt: Wettelijke garantie: geharmoniseerde EU-kennisgeving over de wettelijke conformiteitsgarantie
text: WETTELIJKE GARANTIE
Minimaal twee jaar bescherming dankzij de wettelijke garantie voor goederen die in de Europese Unie worden verkocht.
Consumenten kunnen hun rechten doen gelden op grond van de wettelijke conformiteitsgarantie, bijvoorbeeld als goederen:
niet met de beschrijving overeenstemmen;
niet naar behoren functioneren.

Verkopers zijn aansprakelijk voor elk conformiteitsgebrek dat bestond bij de levering van de goederen en dat binnen de wettelijke garantieperiode aan het licht komt. Verkopers moeten in een dergelijke situatie het volgende aanbieden:
gratis reparatie of gratis vervanging;
in sommige gevallen, gedeeltelijke of volledige terugbetaling.
Sommige landen hebben een langere wettelijke garantieperiode. Voor tweedehandsartikelen kan de garantieperiode korter zijn, maar niet korter dan één jaar.
Als u meer wilt weten over uw rechten in een bepaald land, kunt u de QR-code hieronder scannen of de verkoper om informatie vragen.
europa.eu/youreurope/garantie
Wat moet u doen als u niet-conforme goederen ontvangt:
1. Neem zo spoedig mogelijk contact op met de verkoper om het probleem te melden.
2. Verstrek een aankoopbewijs, zoals een bon, een factuur of een rekeningafschrift.

Verkopers en producenten kunnen ook commerciële garanties aanbieden, die los van de wettelijke garantie van toepassing zijn. Dit GARAN-label bijvoorbeeld staat voor een commerciële levensduurgarantie die kosteloos door de producent wordt aangeboden en het volledige goed dekt.

rules.requirement: Withdrawal from services, subscriptions and dated bookings
rules.shop_must: For services, the 14 days run from the day the contract is concluded; for a subscription to goods, from receipt of the first delivery. To start a paid service within the 14 days, require the consumer's express request and their acknowledgement that the right ends once the service is fully performed. If the consumer then withdraws, they pay an amount in proportion to what was provided until they withdrew, compared with the whole contract, calculated on the total price (the market value if the price is excessive); without the request, or without the information on the right and on this payment, they pay nothing. Once the service is fully performed with that request and acknowledgement, the right of withdrawal ends. Accommodation other than for living, transport of goods, car rental, catering and leisure services for a specific date or period have no right of withdrawal
rules.where_in_shop: Product setup (service or dated booking), checkout boxes for an early start, order confirmation, withdrawal handling
rules.applies_to: Distance and off-premises service contracts with consumers in the EU, including contracts with regular deliveries over a period, as transposed by each country
rules.exemptions: Art. 16(l): accommodation other than for residential purposes, transport of goods, car rental, catering and leisure services with a specific date or period of performance

Date: the 16(a) wording that asks for the request and acknowledgement for paid services comes from Directive (EU) 2019/2161, applied from 28 May 2022; the window, proportional payment and 16(l) exception applied since 13 June 2014. A sales contract with both goods and services counts as a sales contract (Art. 2(5)). The model withdrawal information (Annex I(A)) has an optional sentence on this payment. The withdrawal function itself is in EU-WD-01

Show that person's name and postal and electronic address with the product (on the product page, as EU-PS-01 asks) and on the product, its packaging, the parcel or an accompanying document
rules.applies_to: Shops established outside the EU selling consumer products to buyers in the EU, where the manufacturer is not established in the EU and no EU importer takes the role
rules.exemptions: Product groups outside the GPSR, see GPSR Art. 2(2) (food, medicines, antiques etc.); products covered by other EU harmonisation law follow Art. 4 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 directly
rules.legal_basis: Regulation (EU) 2023/988 (GPSR), Art. 16(1) to (3), with Art. 4(2) and (3) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020
rules.notes: Checked 22 Nov 2026 against the Official Journal text (Publications Office Cellar). GPSR Art. 16(1): a product shall not be placed on the market unless there is an economic operator established in the Union responsible for the Art. 4(3) tasks of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 (keep documents for authorities, answer their requests, report risks, cooperate). Art. 4(2) of 2019/1020 lists who can be that operator. GPSR applies from 13 Dec 2024 (Art. 52). Shopproof cannot act as this person.

rules.requirement: Import VAT on parcels up to EUR 150 (IOSS)
rules.shop_must: For goods shipped from outside the EU to EU consumers in parcels worth up to EUR 150 (not excise goods), choose one way to handle import VAT: register for the Import One-Stop Shop (IOSS), usually through an intermediary established in the EU, and charge the VAT of the buyer's country at checkout so the parcel clears without VAT on delivery; or leave the import VAT to be collected from the buyer on delivery (often with a carrier fee). Above EUR 150, import VAT and customs duty are charged at import. Tell buyers which way you use before they order (see EU-NE-04)
rules.applies_to: Distance sales of goods imported from outside the EU to consumers in the EU, in consignments of an intrinsic value up to EUR 150
rules.exemptions: Products subject to excise duty (alcohol, tobacco, some energy products) are outside IOSS. Goods already stocked in the EU are not imports; their EU distance sales use the Union OSS scheme instead. Sales made through a marketplace that is the deemed supplier are handled by the marketplace
rules.legal_basis: Council Directive 2006/112/EC, Art. 369l to 369x (IOSS) and Art. 369y to 369zb (special arrangements), inserted by Council Directive (EU) 2017/2455, application date set by Council Decision (EU) 2020/1109
rules.notes: Checked 22 Nov 2026 against the Official Journal text (Publications Office Cellar). Art. 369l limits the scheme to consignments of an intrinsic value not exceeding EUR 150, excise goods excluded. Art. 369m(1): sellers not established in the EU use IOSS through an intermediary established in the EU, unless established in a third country with an EU mutual assistance agreement listed by the Commission. Art. 369y: without IOSS, the person presenting the goods to customs (often the carrier) may collect import VAT from the buyer. Decision (EU) 2020/1109 moved the start to 1 July 2021. This is technical help about the rules, not tax advice; a tax adviser should confirm registrations.

rules.requirement: EUR 3 customs duty per item on parcels up to EUR 150
rules.shop_must: From 1 July 2026 the customs duty relief for parcels worth up to EUR 150 is gone. Until 1 July 2028 a flat customs duty of EUR 3 per item applies to such parcels when they go through IOSS or by post; other low-value parcels pay normal customs duty under the Common Customs Tariff. Include this duty in your landed cost and in what you tell buyers before they order
rules.applies_to: Goods shipped from outside the EU to buyers in the EU in consignments of an intrinsic value up to EUR 150
rules.exemptions: None for the sellers concerned. The EUR 3 amount is a temporary measure until 1 July 2028 and the Commission may propose to extend or widen it
rules.legal_basis: Council Regulation (EU) 2026/382, Art. 1 (deletes the threshold-based relief in Regulation (EC) No 1186/2009) and Art. 2 (EUR 3 per item, 1 July 2026 to 1 July 2028)
rules.notes: Checked 22 Nov 2026 against the Official Journal text (Publications Office Cellar). Art. 2: from 1 July 2026 until 1 July 2028 a customs duty of EUR 3 per item in a consignment of intrinsic value not exceeding EUR 150 applies where the import is VAT exempt under Art. 143(1)(ca) of Directive 2006/112/EC (IOSS) or the goods are in a postal consignment. Recital 6: the Common Customs Tariff applies to other operators. Art. 3: monthly review from 1 Oct 2026. Art. 4: applies from 1 July 2026. Watch for an extension before 1 July 2028.

rules.requirement: Import charges in the price shown before the order
rules.shop_must: Before the buyer orders, show the total price including taxes, plus all delivery charges and other costs. If you ship from outside the EU and import VAT, customs duty or carrier fees cannot be included in the price, say clearly before the order that the buyer may have to pay these charges on delivery
rules.where_in_shop: Product page, cart and checkout, before the order button
rules.applies_to: Distance sales to consumers in the EU, including from sellers outside the EU
rules.legal_basis: Directive 2011/83/EU (Consumer Rights Directive), Art. 6(1)(e), with Art. 8(2) for the order page, as transposed by each country
rules.notes: Checked 22 Nov 2026 against the Official Journal text (Publications Office Cellar). Art. 6(1)(e): the total price inclusive of taxes and all additional freight, delivery or postal charges and any other costs or, where those charges cannot reasonably be calculated in advance, the fact that such additional charges may be payable. Applies to contracts concluded after 13 June 2014 (Art. 28(2)). Under Art. 6(1) of Regulation (EC) No 593/2008 (Rome I), a seller who directs its shop at consumers in an EU country is generally bound by that country's consumer law.

rules.shop_must: If your shop is established outside the EU and offers goods or services to people in the EU, designate in writing a representative established in one of the EU countries where your buyers are, and name that representative in your privacy notice
rules.applies_to: Shops established outside the EU that offer goods or services to people in the EU (GDPR Art. 3(2))
rules.exemptions: Not needed for processing that is occasional, does not include large-scale processing of special categories of data or criminal records, and is unlikely to result in a risk to people (Art. 27(2)(a)); a shop that sells to EU buyers regularly will rarely meet this
rules.legal_basis: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR), Art. 3(2) and Art. 27, with Art. 13(1)(a) for naming the representative
rules.notes: Checked 22 Nov 2026 against the Official Journal text (Publications Office Cellar). Art. 27(1): where Art. 3(2) applies, the controller shall designate in writing a representative in the Union; Art. 27(3): established in a Member State where the data subjects are. Art. 13(1)(a) lists the contact details of the controller's representative among the information given to people. The GDPR applies from 25 May 2018 (Art. 99(2)). UK businesses: the UK GDPR has its own representative rule for the UK, separate from this one.

rules.requirement: EUR 2 Union handling fee per item on goods imported in distance sales
rules.shop_must: Since 1 November 2026 customs collect a Union handling fee of EUR 2 per item for each import of goods sold in distance sales from outside the EU, whatever the parcel value and on top of any duty and import VAT. The fee is paid by whoever owes the import duty, usually the declarant (often your carrier or postal operator, who may pass it on to you or the buyer), and it is not refundable. Include it in your landed cost and in what you tell buyers before they order
rules.applies_to: Goods sold to buyers in the EU from outside the EU (distance sales of imported goods under Article 14(4), point (2), of Directive 2006/112/EC) and released for free circulation in the EU
rules.exemptions: A lower amount is planned for goods sold from a customs warehouse for distance sales, from 1 July 2028. The Commission reviews the amount every two years
rules.legal_basis: Regulation (EU) 2026/2108 (Union Customs Code), Art. 20(2), (3), (5) and (6) and Art. 287(4); Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/2152, Art. 1 (EUR 2 per item) and Art. 2 (applies from 1 November 2026)
rules.notes: Checked 22 Nov 2026 against the Official Journal texts (Publications Office Cellar): Reg. 2026/2108 Art. 20(2) Union handling fee of a fixed amount per item for release for free circulation of goods sold in distance sales; Art. 20(5) payable by the debtor of the customs debt at import, or the person who would be; Art. 20(6) non-refundable; Art. 20(4) lower amount for customs warehouses for distance sales applies from 1 July 2028 (Art. 287(5)); Art. 287(4) Art. 20(2) applies 10 days after the delegated act enters into force. Delegated Reg. 2026/2152 (OJ L 22.10.2026) Art. 1 EUR 2 per item, Art. 2 applies from 1 November 2026. Implementing Reg. 2026/2403 adjusts the declaration data for the fee. Separate from the EUR 3 duty in EU-NE-03; both can apply to the same item.

rules.shop_must: Button 'renoncer au contrat ici' (or equivalent); confirm 'confirmer la rétractation'; acknowledgement on durable medium with content, date and time; mention the function in CGV
rules.applies_to: B2C distance contracts via online interface
rules.legal_basis: Code de la consommation L. 221-21, D. 221-5 (Ord. 2026-2, Décret 2026-3)
rules.notes: D. 221-5 read on Légifrance on 3 Nov 2026 (in force since 19 June 2026): the function is labelled 'renoncer au contrat ici' and the confirmation 'confirmer la rétractation', or an equivalent unambiguous wording. L. 221-21 (function, in force 19 June 2026, Ord. 2026-2 art. 26) read the same day. The CCI Paris guide is kept as more info

rules.shop_must: Before the order, inform about the 14 day withdrawal right (droit de rétractation), its conditions, time limit and procedure, and give the model withdrawal form (L. 221-5, 7°); if this information was not given, the period is extended by 12 months (or ends 14 days after the information, if it is given during the extension)
rules.applies_to: Distance and off-premises contracts with consumers in France
rules.exemptions: Exceptions in art. L. 221-28 (custom-made goods, sealed hygiene goods once unsealed, perishables and others)
rules.legal_basis: Code de la consommation, arts. L. 221-5, 7°, L. 221-18 and L. 221-20
rules.notes: L. 221-18 (in force since 1 July 2016, Ord. 2016-301) and L. 221-20 (in force since 28 May 2022) read on Légifrance on 3 Nov 2026; L. 221-5 not read. The date is that of the current article numbering; the same 14 day right applied before under the former articles (loi n° 2014-344), not read here. The withdrawal function is in FR-WD-01

rules.shop_must: Where a contract was concluded online, or the shop offers online contracts when the consumer cancels, offer a free online cancellation function presented as 'résilier votre contrat' (or an equally clear wording, in legible characters), directly and permanently reachable. The consumer enters or checks their identification and contract details, sees a summary page and confirms with 'notifier la résiliation' (or similar). The shop confirms receipt and tells the consumer on a durable medium, within a reasonable time, the date the contract ends and the effects of the cancellation
rules.where_in_shop: Footer / account area, next to the withdrawal button
rules.applies_to: Contracts with consumers and non-professionals that are running (such as subscriptions), concluded online or where the shop offers online contracts, from 1 June 2023
rules.exemptions: None known; check sector rules (insurance, telecoms) separately
rules.legal_basis: Code de la consommation, arts. L. 215-1-1 and D. 215-1 to D. 215-3 (loi n° 2022-1158 du 16 août 2022, art. 15; décret n° 2023-417 du 31 mai 2023)
rules.notes: Légifrance blocks automated readers, so the official texts were not read. L. 215-1-1 read as quoted in full by a law firm (Landot avocats, 5 June 2023); the label 'résilier votre contrat', the three steps and the start date 1 June 2023 taken from the Institut national de la consommation (inc-conso.fr, 20 June 2023), which cites D. 215-1 to D. 215-3. Check the decree on Légifrance before raising confidence. This is cancellation, not withdrawal; the withdrawal function is FR-WD-01

rules.shop_must: Order button must read 'commande avec obligation de paiement' or an equally clear phrase; state accepted payment methods and delivery restrictions at the start of checkout; anyone publishing customer reviews must say whether they are checked and, if so, how, show the review date and give the reasons when a review is rejected
rules.applies_to: All traders
rules.legal_basis: Code de la consommation L. 221-14; L. 111-7-2; D. 111-16 to D. 111-19
rules.notes: Checked 1 Nov 2026 on Légifrance: L. 221-14 in force since 1 July 2016, L. 111-7-2 current version in force since 17 Feb 2024.

rules.shop_must: Button 'recedere dal contratto qui' (or equally clear); confirm 'conferma recesso'; acknowledgement on durable medium; pre-contract info on where the function is
rules.applies_to: B2C distance contracts via online interface
rules.legal_basis: Codice del Consumo art. 54-bis and art. 49(1)(h), D.Lgs. 209/2025

rules.shop_must: Before the order, inform about the 14 day withdrawal right (diritto di recesso), its conditions, time limits and procedure, and give the model withdrawal form (allegato I, parte B); if this information is missing, the period ends 12 months after the normal 14 days (or 14 days after the information, if it is given within those 12 months)
rules.applies_to: Distance and off-premises contracts with consumers in Italy concluded after 13 June 2014
rules.exemptions: Exceptions in art. 59 (custom-made goods, sealed hygiene goods once unsealed, perishables and others)
rules.legal_basis: Codice del consumo (D.Lgs. 206/2005), arts. 49, comma 1, lett. h), 52, 53 and allegato I
rules.notes: Arts. 49, 52 and 53 read on Normattiva on 3 Nov 2026. Date: D.Lgs. 21/2014, art. 2, comma 1 (contracts concluded after 13 June 2014), as noted on Normattiva. Unsolicited doorstep sales have 30 days (art. 52, comma 1-bis); not relevant to online shops. The withdrawal function is in IT-WD-01

rules.shop_must: Button only 'ordine con obbligo di pagare' or equally clear; key info directly before ordering; delivery restrictions and payment methods at the start of checkout
rules.applies_to: All B2C online shops
rules.legal_basis: Codice del Consumo art. 51(2)-(3), as amended by D.Lgs. 30/2026

rules.shop_must: GPSR Art. 19 info with warnings in Italian; fines EUR 2,500-25,000 for operator-duty breaches
rules.applies_to: All sellers to IT consumers

rules.shop_must: Packaging delivered to IT consumers carries material code (Decision 97/129/EC) and disposal guidance; may be provided digitally if the pack or online point of sale says where to find it
rules.applies_to: Packaging placed on the Italian market incl. e-commerce boxes
rules.notes: Digital route details from secondary summaries; watch PPWR decree

rules.shop_must: Inform consumers clearly, e.g. on the website, that take-back of the old appliance is free; 1:1 take-back on delivery
rules.applies_to: Distributors incl. online sellers of EEE

rules.shop_must: Function with a clear label, e.g. 'hier de overeenkomst ontbinden' or 'hier de overeenkomst herroepen'; confirm e.g. 'ontbinding bevestigen'; acknowledgement with date and time
rules.applies_to: B2C distance contracts via online interface
rules.notes: No exact wording prescribed; examples from explanatory memorandum

rules.shop_must: Before the order, inform about the 14 day right of withdrawal (recht van ontbinding, also called herroepingsrecht), its conditions, time limit and procedure, and give the model withdrawal form; if this information is missing, the period is extended until it is given, by at most 12 months
rules.applies_to: Distance and off-premises contracts with consumers in the Netherlands
rules.exemptions: Exceptions in art. 6:230p BW (custom-made goods, sealed hygiene goods once unsealed, perishables and others)
rules.legal_basis: Burgerlijk Wetboek Boek 6, arts. 230m lid 1 onder h, 230o and 230p
rules.notes: Arts. 6:230m, 6:230o and 6:230p read on wetten.overheid.nl (version in force from 16 July 2026) on 3 Nov 2026. Unlike the directive wording, art. 6:230o lid 2 extends the period by the time until the information is given, at most 12 months. Date: the directive application date; the Dutch commencement decree was not read. The withdrawal function is in NL-WD-01

rules.shop_must: GPSR warnings, safety information and recall notices at least in Dutch
rules.applies_to: All sellers to NL consumers
rules.legal_basis: Warenwetbesluit uitvoering verordening algemene productveiligheid, art. 3

rules.requirement: Point to WEEE take-back before purchase
rules.shop_must: Offer free 1:1 take-back of an equivalent old appliance and clearly point the consumer to the options before purchase and before delivery
rules.applies_to: Distributors incl. distance sellers of EEE

rules.shop_must: Notify Rijkswaterstaat within 6 weeks (or join producer organisation); foreign producers appoint NL representative; inform customers how to return textiles free
rules.applies_to: Sellers of new clothing and household textiles to NL
rules.notes: From about 2028: footwear added, public register, mandatory producer organisation

rules.shop_must: Order button stating payment obligation, e.g. 'bestelling met betalingsverplichting'; delivery restrictions and payment methods at start of checkout
